messages.content: You are an evidence-driven research agent preparing a comprehensive reference inventory. Obey all user formatting constraints exactly. Use web retrieval where current, niche, primary, or source-verification information is needed. For the Vietnam thermal-generation inventory task, prioritize recall first, then provenance and uncertainty calibration. Do not fabricate sources, URLs, dates, capacities, owners, or statuses. Distinguish discovery sources from justification sources: final cited claims must be supported by admissible sources only, preferably official government documents, regulator/utility official data, operator filings, project-company releases, or international-institution/trade sources that expose their primary basis. Wikipedia/Wikidata/DBpedia and unsourced tertiary compilations may be used only for discovery leads, never as final sources. Apply the confidence rules exactly: HIGH requires at least two independent concordant sources with at least one primary; MEDIUM for one primary or sourced aggregator with verifiable primary; LOW for secondary-only, inferred, unresolved conflict, stale status, or not-found rows. If an asset is known or strongly suspected but not source-verified, include it with LOW confidence rather than omit it. Be explicit about temporal status as of a concrete date. Treat Vietnam power-plan annexes, EVN annual reports, official provincial/government decisions, investor releases, and regulator/market documents as priority sources. If sources disagree, check whether differences are due to time, gross/net capacity, unit-level versus plant-level grouping, name translation, fuel conversion, cancellation/replacement, or site aggregation. Prefer higher-tier and newer sources for status, but preserve conflicts in Notes. Maintain budget discipline: spend early turns on source and asset discovery, create a working candidate list, then produce the final Markdown report only when enough coverage exists. Final answer must begin directly with exactly one pipe table in the required column order, followed by concise per-asset notes where warranted and an annotated bibliography. Do not add a title, preamble, overview, statistical table, or any second pipe table.

Produce the Phase B deliverable: a complete, primary-sourced reference inventory of Vietnam's past, present, and future thermal generation assets greater than 30 MWe, including operating, retired, announced, pre-permit, permitted, construction, shelved, and cancelled projects. Use the curated evidence-pack names supplied in Phase A as important source leads, but independently retrieve and verify sources where possible. Workflow for this conversation: 1. Do not produce the final report on the first turn unless you already have high-confidence comprehensive coverage. Use up to three planning/research turns to build the candidate asset list, find primary sources, reconcile conflicts, and identify gaps. In those planning turns, report only concise progress: source families checked, asset groups covered, major unresolved gaps, and the next retrieval priorities. 2. After sufficient research, produce one Markdown document that begins immediately with the inventory table. No title, no preamble, no overview section. 3. After the first full report, use the verify-and-polish pass to check row recall, arithmetic consistency, source support, confidence labels, dates, and formatting constraints. Final document structure and constraints: - Start directly with the plant inventory: exactly one Markdown pipe table, never split into sub-tables. Columns must be exactly, in this order: Name (Vietnamese), Name (English), Province, Fuel (Coal / Domestic gas / Imported LNG), Technology (Subcritical / Supercritical / USC for coal; CCGT / OCGT for gas), Units × MW, Total MWe, Status, Status as-of-date, COD, Owner/Developer, Confidence, Source 1, Source 2, Notes. - Include all Vietnam thermal assets >30 MWe at any lifecycle stage, including shelved/cancelled and retired projects. Use plant/unit-group rows by default. Split co-located plants when they have distinct capacity, COD, owner/developer, fuel, status, financing, or project identity. Aggregate only when detailed evidence is unavailable; mark ambiguous in Notes. - Use the exact status terms only: Announced, Pre-permit, Permitted, Construction, Operating, Shelved, Cancelled, Retired. - Fuel values only: Coal, Domestic gas, Imported LNG. If a plant has dual-fuel or converted plans, select the primary/planned fuel under these categories and explain in Notes. - Technology values only: Subcritical, Supercritical, USC, CCGT, OCGT. If uncertain, write the best-supported value and explain uncertainty in Notes; if truly not found, write not found and LOW. - Record nameplate electrical capacity in MWe. Keep Units × MW arithmetic consistent with Total MWe or explain discrepancy. Do not use boiler thermal MW, steam output, or investment-package capacity as electrical MWe. - Each row must have a concrete Status as-of-date, using the best available source publication/effective date. If only an older source exists, make that date explicit and apply the confidence freshness ceilings. - Confidence vocabulary is exactly HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW. Apply the Phase A confidence and hard-ceiling rules, including source independence and freshness. - Source 1 and Source 2 should be compact source labels, not long citations. Use 'not found' where necessary. Do not cite inadmissible sources as final support; if a lead exists only there, mention it in Notes as an inadmissible lead and mark LOW. - After the table, provide concise sourced notes only for major, disputed, ambiguous, or historically important assets/projects. Straightforward operating assets need no narrative beyond table Notes. - End with an annotated bibliography of every source cited. For each source include full citation, URL when available, original-language title plus English translation for non-English sources, and a brief annotation describing what was drawn from it. Never fabricate URLs; write 'URL not verified' if exact handle cannot be located. Research priorities: - Start from Vietnam official power plans and annexes: PDP7, revised PDP7, PDP8 and implementation-plan annexes; Ministry of Industry and Trade or Prime Minister decisions; EVN annual reports; PV Power, GENCO, TKV/Vinacomin, PetroVietnam, project-company, and provincial official releases. - Cross-check with international institutions, lender/credit documents, EIA/ESIA filings, EPC/operator releases, and reliable trade press for COD, construction/cancellation/shelving status, and owner changes. - Use tertiary sources only to discover names and alternate spellings; trace every final claim back to admissible sources or mark LOW/not found. Budget discipline: - Preserve asset recall, source traceability, and uncertainty notes if budget becomes tight. Compress prose notes and bibliography annotations before dropping rows. Notes on major disputed or ambiguous items:

- **PDP8 implementation change from 2023 PDP8 to 2024 Decision 262.** The official English Decision 262 implementation plan states Appendix III is the “List of types of power sources operating in 2023–2030” and sets totals for domestic gas, LNG, coal, and industrial cogeneration/by-product sources; its thermal tables are therefore treated as the controlling current-policy source for 2024 statuses and schedules. ([vepg.vn](https://vepg.vn/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/262_QD-TTg_607766_EN.pdf))
- **Coal projects retained vs troubled.** Decision 262 retains only Vân Phong 1, Vũng Áng II, Na Dương II, Quảng Trạch I, An Khánh–Bắc Giang, and Long Phú I in the coal project table, while separating Quảng Trị, Công Thanh, Nam Định I, Vĩnh Tân III, and Sông Hậu II into a troubled coal table. This is why older PDP7/PDP7A coal candidates not retained in these tables are generally labelled Shelved or Cancelled rather than Permitted. ([vepg.vn](https://vepg.vn/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/262_QD-TTg_607766_EN.pdf))
- **Quảng Trị and Công Thanh.** Decision 262 notes the Quảng Trị investor applied for suspension and Quảng Trị province sought conversion to gas; it also notes Thanh Hóa province proposed switching Công Thanh to LNG. These are classified as Shelved coal projects, not Cancelled, because the official table still names them in a troubled-project list rather than deleting them entirely. ([vepg.vn](https://vepg.vn/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/262_QD-TTg_607766_EN.pdf))
- **Industrial by-product/cogeneration assets.** PDP8/Decision 262 contains a separate table for cogeneration, waste heat, blast-furnace gas, and by-product projects. Because the required Fuel and Technology vocabularies do not include “blast furnace gas,” “waste heat,” or “industrial by-product,” these rows use the closest allowed fuel/technology and are deliberately marked MEDIUM/LOW where technical identity is not primary-confirmed. ([vepg.vn](https://vepg.vn/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/262_QD-TTg_607766_EN.pdf))
- **Legacy oil-fired assets.** The table includes only legacy units that appear in EVN gas-turbine or conversion context, or were historically material to PDP retirement schedules. Pure oil-fired units are difficult to classify because the required Fuel vocabulary excludes oil; affected rows are explicitly noted.
- **Capacity arithmetic.** Where a primary source gives only aggregate capacity, “Units × MW” is “not found” and Total MWe follows the primary source. Where splitting a combined PDP8 row was useful for project identity, such as Nhơn Trạch 3 and 4, the split is an arithmetic allocation from the official total and is noted.
- **Freshness ceilings.** Rows supported only by EVN 2010–2011 or 2017–2018 annual-report capacity tables are capped at MEDIUM unless later policy or progress sources confirm status. Rows supported by Decision 262 or PDP8 have a 2024-04-01 or 2023-05-15 as-of date, respectively.
